terms.definition: The movement of an element between living organisms and the atmosphere, hydrosphere and lithosphere.
terms.examiner: Be able to name the reservoirs and the processes that move the element between them.

terms.definition: The conversion of nitrogen gas into ammonia or nitrates, by bacteria, lightning or the Haber process.
terms.examiner: Rhizobium in the root nodules of legumes is the usual biological example.

terms.definition: The oxidation of ammonium ions to nitrites and then nitrates by bacteria in aerobic soil.
terms.examiner: Needs oxygen, so waterlogging slows it.

terms.definition: The conversion of nitrates to nitrogen gas by bacteria in anaerobic conditions.
terms.examiner: Reduces soil fertility; drainage reduces it.

terms.definition: Nutrient enrichment of water, leading to algal growth, death and decomposition of the algae, and deoxygenation.
terms.examiner: Give the sequence in order; the fish die from lack of oxygen, not from the nutrients.

terms.definition: The average time an atom or molecule stays in a reservoir.
terms.examiner: Short residence times mean a reservoir responds quickly to change.

terms.definition: Fungi living in association with plant roots that increase the uptake of phosphates.
terms.examiner: Important because phosphates are not very soluble and move slowly in soil.
